messages:
alex: FYI I noticed the /v1/embed endpoint examples use an object for the request batch in some places (`{ inputs: { text: ... } }`) while other examples and the SDK expect an array (`[ { text: ... } ]`). support just pinged about users getting 422s when they paste the object example.

rachel: thanks. where did you see the object variant? openapi examples or generated snippets?

alex: both. there9s an OpenAPI example file and the small curl/python snippets in the quickstart. the server accepts an array of inputs; the object form was a stale example from an early draft.

mike: I can patch. plan: update OpenAPI example to use `inputs: [{"text":"..."}]`, change curl/python/js snippets, and add a short note in the parameter description: "inputs: array[object] — do not pass a single object."

rachel: sgtm. also add a migration-note line in the embeddings migration guide: many users embed lists vs single items, better to show both patterns but emphasize array is canonical.

alex: good call. add a test in docs CI that loads examples and validates against the OpenAPI schema. we9ve had drift like this before.

mike: added a small script call and updated docs CI job. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4301 1: updated examples, changed snippets, added migration note.

ci-bot: docs-ci started for PR 4301 (:building_construction:)

rachel: quick nit: in the python snippet you left `inputs = {"text": "..."}` in one place. please switch to a list and include a comment `# single-item batch: use [item] not item`.

mike: fixed and pushed.

ci-bot: docs-ci passed for PR 4301 (:white_check_mark:) 7: https://ci.internal.redwood/4301

alex: approved. can we also add an example showing server-side batching best practices (send as array of items) and note that legacy single-object examples are invalid?

rachel: yep adding a short paragraph under "Batching and request shapes".

mike: merged, cherry-picked to `1.x` branch since a couple customers were on pinned docs.

alex: thanks — that'll reduce the support noise.

rachel: great catch alex. please flag if you see any other example drift.
